title: Exact Breit-Rabi formulae for the nitrogen-vacancy center in diamond
authors: Alex Tritt, Lincoln D. Turner, Michael S. J. Barson
abstract: The hyperfine structure that the nitrogen-vacancy (NV) center in diamond has with its nitrogen nucleus is of immense importance for quantum sensing and quantum computing. Current methods of calculating the NV hyperfine energy eigenvalues and eigenstates with respect to an axial magnetic field - i.e., calculating the NV Breit-Rabi formula - resort to numerical methods and analytic approximations. Here we provide an exact, closed-form expression to the NV hyperfine energy eigenvalues and eigenstates for both the nitrogen-14 and -15 cases.
summary: This paper derives exact, closed-form Breit-Rabi formulae for the energy levels and eigenstates of the NV center in diamond for both $^{14}	ext{N}$ and $^{15}	ext{N}$. By providing these analytic solutions, the authors improve upon existing numerical and approximate methods, which is vital for high-precision quantum sensing and quantum computing applications.
main_problem: To derive exact, closed-form expressions for the energy eigenvalues and eigenstates of the Nitrogen-Vacancy (NV) center in diamond under an axial magnetic field.
main_result: The authors provide analytic, closed-form solutions for the energy levels and eigenstates for both $^{14}	ext{N}$ and $^{15}	ext{N}$ isotopes, surpassing previous numerical or approximate methods.
method: The derivation involves solving the characteristic polynomial of the spin Hamiltonian, utilizing trigonometric and algebraic techniques to find exact roots and corresponding eigenstates.
model_or_system: The physical system is the NV center in diamond, modeled by a fine-structure spin Hamiltonian incorporating Zero-Field Splitting (D) and hyperfine coupling terms for both the electron spin ($S=1$) and the nitrogen nuclear spin ($I=1$ or $I=1/2$).
key_observables: Energy eigenvalues ($\lambda_j$ or $E_n$) and the corresponding eigenstates ($\psi_j$ or $|\psi_nangle$), particularly focusing on level anticrossings (GSLAC, ESLAC).
important_parameters: Zero-Field Splitting ($D$), hyperfine coupling constants ($A_{\parallel}, A_{\perp}$), and the magnetic field components ($\gamma, \gamma_I, B_z$).
main_assumptions: The initial Hamiltonian is assumed to be solvable analytically, although approximations (like quadratic expansions) are used to analyze specific regimes such as anticrossings.
figures_summary: Figures compare the derived analytic eigenvalues and eigenvectors against point-wise numerical evaluations for both $^{14}	ext{N}$ and $^{15}	ext{N}$ centers, demonstrating agreement across different magnetic field regimes.
paper_structure: The paper systematically addresses the problem for both $^{15}	ext{N}$ and $^{14}	ext{N}$ isotopes, deriving the Hamiltonian matrix, solving the resulting characteristic equations using advanced mathematical techniques, and finally applying the results to predict key spectroscopic features like level anticrossings.
why_interesting: This work provides fundamental, exact theoretical tools for understanding spin dynamics in solid-state quantum systems, which is crucial for designing robust quantum sensors and qubits based on NV centers.

FIG. 3. Comparison between our derived analytic eigen- values (colored dots) and point wise numerical evaluations (black lines) for the 15N center at the GSLAC. Numbers on the right refer to the state labels of Eq. (B1). Derived ana- lytic curves and numerical evaluations were confirmed to be equal to float64 precision [23].

FIG. 4. Comparison between our derived analytic eigenvec- tors of Eq. (B2) (colored dots) and point wise numerical eval- uations (black lines) for the 15N center at the GSLAC. Each sub-figure corresponds to a different eigenstate of Eq. (B2), in ascending order of |1⟩at the top and |6⟩on the bottom. Each curve corresponds to the coefficient of the |mS, mI⟩la- beled on the right, with only non-zero coefficients are shown. Derived analytic coefficients and numerical evaluations were confirmed to be equal to float64 precision [23].

FIG. 5. Comparison between our derived analytic eigen- values (colored dots) and point wise numerical evaluations (black lines) for the 14N center at the GSLAC. Numbers on the right refer to the state labels of Eq. (C1). Errors (bottom) are the absolute difference of the two evaluations, shown on a log scale. Derived analytic curves and numerical evaluations were confirmed to be equal to float64 precision [23].
